chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the one in Ihram who touches perfume while he is asleep and does not know. He said: 'He should wash it, and there is nothing upon him.' And about the one in Ihram who is anointed by the one not in Ihram with aromatic oil, and the one in Ihram does not know what is upon him. He said: 'He should wash it as well, and let him be cautious.'

key_terms.الْحَلَال: The one not in Ihram (permissible state)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِم: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ: There is nothing upon him (no expiation required)
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُ: He washes it (the area of contact)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who touches perfume while asleep?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that unintentional contact with perfume while in Ihram, whether by touch or anointing, does not incur a penalty (kaffarah) but requires washing the affected area. The Imam’s instruction to 'be cautious' (waliyhadhar) highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on distinguishing between mere ritual impurity requiring purification and actual liability for expiation, reinforcing the principle of ease in cases of ignorance or sleep.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam touching the perfume and he is asleep. Heasws said: ‘He should wash it, and there is nothing upon him (to expiate)’. And about the one in Ihraam being massaged by the one not in Ihraam, with the aromatic oil, and the one in Ihraam does not know what is upon him. Heasws said: ‘He should wash it as well, and let him be cautious’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar who has said the following: “I once asked ibn abu ‘Umayr about apple, citron and lotus and things with sweet fragrance. He said, ‘Hold back from smelling while you eat them.’” (It seems like it is ibn abu ‘Umayr’s Fatwa)
